summary: This rule tells the web server to permanently redirect any URL that starts with '/category/' to the same path without that '/category/' prefix. For example, a request to '/category/products' would redirect to '/products'. The '301' status code tells browsers and search engines this is a permanent move, so they should update their bookmarks and search indexes accordingly.

explanations.1: RedirectMatch uses a pattern (the part between the ^ and $) to match URLs, and 301 means 'permanently moved'. The (.*) captures everything after '/category/' in parentheses, and $1 in the target URL refers back to that captured part, effectively removing the '/category/' prefix.
